bd-chronology.title: Bible Chronology (Introduction; Chronology of the Old Testament)
bd-chronology.author: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
bd-chronology.publisher: Intellectual Reserve, Inc. (Bible Dictionary appendix, King James Version study helps)
bd-chronology.read: Introduction page and the full Old Testament table, from the patriarchs through the Persian period.
bd-chronology.limits: Older chronology: the first date column follows Kings and Chronicles (e.g., Saul 1095 BC, division 975 BC); a 'Rev. Chr.' column gives revised dates from Assyrian records. No dates before Saul; calls the Judges dates 'very uncertain'. Read through the Church content API.

ot-instructors-appendix-b.title: Appendix B: Chronological Correlation of the Kings of Israel and of Judah
ot-instructors-appendix-b.author: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (Church Educational System)
ot-instructors-appendix-b.publisher: Intellectual Reserve, Inc., Old Testament Instructor's Guide, Religion 301-2
ot-instructors-appendix-b.read: Full reign table, Rehoboam and Jeroboam I through Zedekiah, with scripture references and the closing note.
ot-instructors-appendix-b.limits: Says the dates are 'a consensus of commonly held views of scholars', approximate, and may differ slightly from other chronologies. Names no chronology system; it uses co-regencies and runs about one year after Thiele (930 vs 931). Starts at 930 BC; no Saul, David, or Solomon dates.

hayes-yale-lecture-6.title: Lecture 6 - Biblical Narrative: The Stories of the Patriarchs (Genesis 12-36)
hayes-yale-lecture-6.author: Christine Hayes
hayes-yale-lecture-6.publisher: Yale University, Open Yale Courses, RLST 145 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
hayes-yale-lecture-6.read: Transcript sections on archaeology and the historicity of the patriarchal stories.
hayes-yale-lecture-6.limits: Lecture overview of scholarly views; no fixed dates for the patriarchs.

hayes-yale-lecture-7.title: Lecture 7 - Israel in Egypt: Moses and the Beginning of Yahwism (Genesis 37 - Exodus 4)
hayes-yale-lecture-7.author: Christine Hayes
hayes-yale-lecture-7.publisher: Yale University, Open Yale Courses, RLST 145 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
hayes-yale-lecture-7.read: Transcript section on the historical value and date of the Exodus (Merneptah Stele, Hyksos theory, the 480 years of 1 Kings 6:1).
hayes-yale-lecture-7.limits: Lecture, not a full argument; her 1265 BCE figure is an illustrative calculation.

hayes-yale-lecture-12.title: Lecture 12 - The Deuteronomistic History: Life in the Land (Joshua and Judges)
hayes-yale-lecture-12.author: Christine Hayes
hayes-yale-lecture-12.publisher: Yale University, Open Yale Courses, RLST 145 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
hayes-yale-lecture-12.read: Transcript sections on the archaeology of the conquest and the immigration, revolt, and internal-development models.
hayes-yale-lecture-12.limits: Lecture overview; no exact dates for Joshua's campaigns.

hayes-yale-lecture-13.title: Lecture 13 - The Deuteronomistic History: Prophets and Kings (1 and 2 Samuel)
hayes-yale-lecture-13.author: Christine Hayes
hayes-yale-lecture-13.publisher: Yale University, Open Yale Courses, RLST 145 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
hayes-yale-lecture-13.read: Transcript section introducing the setting of Judges.
hayes-yale-lecture-13.limits: Gives only a round period for Judges (about 1200 to 1000).

hayes-yale-lecture-22.title: Lecture 22 - The Restoration: 1 and 2 Chronicles, Ezra and Nehemiah
hayes-yale-lecture-22.author: Christine Hayes
hayes-yale-lecture-22.publisher: Yale University, Open Yale Courses, RLST 145 Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
hayes-yale-lecture-22.read: Transcript sections on Cyrus (539/538), the 597 exiles, the temple rebuilding (about 515), Nehemiah (about 445), and the problem of dating Ezra.
hayes-yale-lecture-22.limits: Lecture overview; does not name a specific alternative year for Ezra.

britannica-saul.limits: Encyclopedia summary; reign dates approximate (c. 1021-1000 BCE). WebFetch was blocked (403); page read with curl.

bibleodyssey-saul.title: Saul

bibleodyssey-saul.limits: Discusses whether Saul was a king; gives no reign years.

genesis.label: Undated (primeval history)
genesis.note: The Bible Dictionary lists Adam to Babel without dates. It says early dates cannot be fixed with certainty.

genesis.label: Undated (ancestral stories)
genesis.note: The Bible Dictionary gives no dates for the patriarchs. Hayes reports a scholarly debate about how much history the stories hold.

genesis.label: Undated (Joseph story)
genesis.note: Hayes calls a Hyksos-period setting for Joseph a hypothesis that is not well supported. The Bible Dictionary gives no date.

exodus.label: ~1300 - 1200 BCE (disputed)
exodus.note: Hayes and Britannica place a possible Exodus in the 13th century BCE. The 480 years of 1 Kings 6:1 point earlier; Hayes calls that number ideal. Historicity is debated.

leviticus.label: ~1300 - 1200 BCE (disputed)
leviticus.note: The laws are set at Sinai, in the Exodus setting. Hayes and Britannica favor the 13th century BCE; an earlier date rests on 1 Kings 6:1.

numbers.label: ~1300 - 1200 BCE (disputed)
numbers.note: The wilderness years follow the Exodus setting. Hayes allows 40 years of travel in a 13th-century reconstruction. An earlier date rests on 1 Kings 6:1.

deuteronomy.label: ~1300 - 1200 BCE (disputed)
deuteronomy.note: The speeches are set at the end of the wilderness period. The setting follows the disputed Exodus date.

joshua.label: ~1250 - 1200 BCE (disputed)
joshua.note: Hayes places new highland settlements in the late 13th century. The Merneptah Stele (~1204) puts Israel in Canaan. Archaeology does not show Joshua's conquest.

judges.label: ~1200 - 1000 BCE
judges.note: Hayes sets Judges in a period from about 1200 to 1000. The Bible Dictionary says the order and dates of the judges are very uncertain.

ruth.label: ~1200 - 1000 BCE
ruth.note: Ruth 1:1 sets the story when the judges ruled. Hayes dates that period about 1200 to 1000; no source gives a closer date.

1-samuel.label: ~1100 - 1000 BCE
1-samuel.note: Eli and Samuel come before Saul. Britannica dates Saul to the 11th century BCE; no source dates these chapters more closely.

1-samuel.label: ~1021 - 1000 BCE
1-samuel.note: Britannica dates Saul's reign about 1021-1000 BCE. The older Bible Dictionary table starts it in 1095. Bible Odyssey notes his kingship is debated.

2-samuel.label: ~1000 - 970 BCE
2-samuel.note: Britannica says David flourished about 1000 BCE. Saul's reign ends about 1000; Solomon's 40 years end near 930. Exact years vary by chronology.

1-kings.label: ~970 BCE
1-kings.note: David dies and Solomon takes the throne. Sources place Solomon in the 10th century; ~970 counts his 40 years back from 930.

1-kings.label: ~970 - 930 BCE
1-kings.note: Bible Odyssey places Solomon in the mid-10th century. The Church reign table starts Rehoboam in 930. Britannica notes archaeological debate.

1-kings.label: ~930 - 909 BCE
1-kings.note: Rehoboam 930-913 and Jeroboam I 930-909 in the Church reign table, which reflects common scholarly views.

1-kings.label: ~913 - 874 BCE
1-kings.note: Abijam (913) through Omri (885-874) and Ahab's accession, in the Church reign table.

1-kings.label: ~874 - 853 BCE
1-kings.note: Elijah's stories fall in Ahab's reign, 874-853 in the Church reign table.

1-kings.label: ~853 - 848 BCE
1-kings.note: Ahab dies (853). The chapter ends with Jehoshaphat (to 848) and Ahaziah of Israel (853-852).

2-kings.label: ~852 BCE
2-kings.note: Ahaziah of Israel reigns 853-852 in the Church reign table.

2-kings.label: ~852 - 841 BCE
2-kings.note: Elisha's stories fall mainly under Joram of Israel, 852-841. Chapter 8 also covers Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah, to 841.

2-kings.label: ~841 BCE
2-kings.note: Jehu's revolt kills Joram and Ahaziah in 841.

2-kings.label: ~841 - 814 BCE
2-kings.note: Jehu reigns 841-814 in the Church reign table.

2-kings.label: ~814 - 753 BCE
2-kings.note: Jehoahaz (814) to the death of Jeroboam II (753) in the Church reign table. The old end year matched no listed reign.

2-kings.label: ~792 - 732 BCE
2-kings.note: Azariah's reign starts 792 as co-regent in the Church table; 767 was his sole reign. Hoshea's coup is 732. Both tables call these numbers uncertain.

2-kings.label: ~735 - 715 BCE
2-kings.note: Ahaz reigns 735-715 in the Church reign table.

2-kings.label: ~732 - 722 BCE
2-kings.note: Hoshea reigns 732-722. Both Church tables end the northern kingdom in 722.

2-kings.label: ~715 - 701 BCE
2-kings.note: Hezekiah's accession (about 715) to Sennacherib's 701 campaign. Britannica notes a wide range of possible reign dates.

2-kings.label: ~701 - 681 BCE
2-kings.note: The siege is 701. Verse 37 reports Sennacherib's death, which both sources date to 681. This matches Isaiah 37.

2-kings.label: ~715 - 686 BCE
2-kings.note: The illness and the Babylonian envoys match Isaiah 38-39 (~715-701, ~704-703). Hezekiah dies about 686.

2-kings.label: ~640 - 622 BCE
2-kings.note: Josiah's accession (about 640) to his eighteenth year (22:3), about 622.

2-kings.label: ~622 - 609 BCE
2-kings.note: Josiah's reform to his death in 609. The chapter ends with Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim, both from 609.

2-kings.label: ~609 - 597 BCE
2-kings.note: Jehoiakim 609-598, Jehoiachin 598-597, then the 597 exile and Zedekiah's accession.

2-kings.label: ~588 - 561 BCE
2-kings.note: The siege starts in Zedekiah's ninth year. Jerusalem falls in 587/586. The Bible Dictionary dates Jehoiachin's release to 561.

1-chronicles.label: Undated (genealogies)
1-chronicles.note: Genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles. The lists cover many periods and have no single date.

1-chronicles.label: ~1000 BCE
1-chronicles.note: Saul's death. Britannica ends his reign about 1000 BCE.

1-chronicles.label: ~1000 - 970 BCE
1-chronicles.note: David's reign, to Solomon's accession. Britannica says David flourished about 1000 BCE. Exact years vary by chronology.

2-chronicles.label: ~970 - 930 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Solomon's reign. The Church reign table starts Rehoboam in 930.

2-chronicles.label: ~930 - 913 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Rehoboam reigns 930-913 in the Church reign table. Thiele's 931 differs by one year.

2-chronicles.label: ~913 - 910 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Abijah (Abijam) reigns 913-910 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~910 - 869 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Asa reigns 910-869 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~872 - 848 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Jehoshaphat reigns 872-848, with co-regency, in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~853 - 835 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Jehoram of Judah 853-841 (with co-regency), Ahaziah 841, and Athaliah 841-835.

2-chronicles.label: ~835 - 796 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Joash reigns 835-796 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~796 - 767 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Amaziah reigns 796-767 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~792 - 740 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Uzziah reigns 792-740, with co-regency, in the Church reign table. 767 was the start of his sole reign.

2-chronicles.label: ~750 - 732 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Jotham reigns 750-732, with co-regencies, in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~735 - 715 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Ahaz reigns 735-715 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~715 - 686 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Hezekiah's reforms start in his first year (29:3). His reign is often dated about 715-686.

2-chronicles.label: ~701 - 681 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Sennacherib's campaign is 701. Verse 21 reports his death in 681. This matches Isaiah 37.

2-chronicles.label: ~697 - 640 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Manasseh 697-642 and Amon 642-640 in the Church reign table.

2-chronicles.label: ~609 - 538 BCE
2-chronicles.note: Jehoahaz (609) to Cyrus's decree. Hayes dates the fall of Babylon to 539 and the return to after 538.

ezra.label: ~538 - 515 BCE
ezra.note: The return after Cyrus's decree (538) to the temple dedication, about 515 in Hayes. Ezra 4:6-23 inserts later letters.

ezra.label: ~458 BCE (disputed)
ezra.note: The Bible Dictionary dates Ezra's commission to 458 under Artaxerxes I. Hayes notes a later Artaxerxes is possible, so experts disagree.

nehemiah.label: ~445 - 432 BCE
nehemiah.note: Nehemiah arrives about 445 (Hayes) or 444 (Britannica, Bible Dictionary). He governs 12 years (Neh 5:14), to about 432.

nehemiah.label: ~432 BCE or later
nehemiah.note: The Bible Dictionary dates the second mission to 432. Nehemiah 13:6 gives no exact interval, and no source gives an end year.

esther.label: ~483 - 473 BCE (setting)
esther.note: The story is set under Xerxes I (486-465), in his third to twelfth years. Britannica finds no consensus on a historical basis.
